research_rationale:
Executive Order 11851 of April 10, 1975 (40 FR 16645), Delegation of Authority To Issue Regulations Limiting Imports of Certain Cheeses, is issued under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1854), and 3 U.S.C. 301. Section 1 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to implement an agreement concluded in December 1974 with the Commission of the European Communities by issuing regulations (a) preventing importation into the Customs Territory of the United States, except Puerto Rico, of certain European Communities cheeses on which restitution payments have been made for export to Puerto Rico, other possessions or any country other than the United States, and (b) preventing importation of such cheeses into Puerto Rico for transshipment elsewhere in the Customs Territory. Section 2 authorizes heads of departments and agencies to redelegate, with the Treasury regulation-issuing function redelegable only to officials appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, as 3 U.S.C. 301 provides. The packet's machine inventory merged section 2 into subsection (b) and left a fragment '301.' as a fourth clause, so I corrected the inventory into four clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text (section 1 lead-in and recital, subsection (a), subsection (b), section 2). Search of held texts for the number EO 11851 finds only the order, the 1989 OFR codification (no amendment or revocation) and 19 CFR 12.6; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report only machine hits for the U.S. Code note and 19 CFR 12.6, none of which ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The held text of 19 CFR 12.6 (eCFR searched point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) names the order. The order's own text states no end date, event or condition; the December 1974 agreement is its purpose, not a condition of its continuance, and no held source shows that agreement ended. All four clauses are operative as of 2026-10-14.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) 
of the Immigration and Nationality Act, as amended (8 U.S.C. 1182(f) and 
1185(a)(1)), and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, and in order

to migration of undocumented aliens in the Caribbean region, it is hereby 
ordered: 
Section 1. Duties and Authorities of Agency Heads. Consistent with applica-
ble law, 
(a)(i) The Attorney General may maintain custody, at any location he 
deems appropriate, of any undocumented aliens he has reason to believe 
are seeking to enter the United States and who are interdicted or intercepted 
in the Caribbean region. In this regard, the Attorney General shall provide 
and operate a facility, or facilities, to house and provide for the needs 
of any such aliens. Such a facility may be located at Guantanamo Bay 
Naval Base or any other appropriate location. 
(ii) The Attorney General may conduct any screening of such aliens that 
he deems appropriate, including screening to determine whether such aliens 
should be returned to their country of origin or transit, or whether they 
are persons in need of protection who should not be returned without 
their consent. If the Attorney General institutes such screening, then until 
a determination is made, the Attorney General shall provide for the custody, 
care, safety, transportation, and other needs of the aliens. The Attorney 
General shall continue to provide for the custody, care, safety, transportation, 
and other needs of aliens who are determined not to be persons in need 
of protection until such time as they are returned to their country of origin 
or transit. 
(b) The Secretary of State shall provide for the custody, care, safety, 
transportation, and other needs of undocumented aliens interdicted or inter-
cepted in the Caribbean region whom the Attorney General has identified

Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; I corrected it to 13 clauses by merging the 14-character section 3 heading into section 3(a), and the entries 'lead' (the authority recital) and 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067), Federal Physicians Comparability Allowance, has two numbered sections in the held Federal Register text. Section 1-101 is therefore operative as of 2026-10-14.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The paragraph establishes the Good Conduct Medal and authorizes its award to enlisted members under regulations of the service Secretaries. Before EO 9323: Army enlisted men who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal service and are recommended by their commanders, regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 9323: restated; Army enlisted men who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years, or after December 7, 1941 served one year during war; no commander recommendation; regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 10444: restated; authority as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces; regulations by the Secretaries of the Army and the Air Force; Army and Air Force enlisted men; adds those with less than three years of honorable service after June 27, 1950 who were not previously awarded the medal; proviso against awards for less than one year except physical-disability separations. After EO 14085 section 2: men becomes members and Space Force is added with a December 20, 2019 start for Space Force members. The clause was amended, never ended, and the U.S. Code prints the amended text as current, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (6 FR 3209), Good Conduct Medal, is a single operative paragraph in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8809.txt; trailing number [No. 8809], signed Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House June 28, 1941): a Good Conduct Medal is established and may be awarded, under regulations of the Secretary of War, to enlisted men of the Army of the United States who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal military service and are recommended by their commanding officers. Three later orders each amend that single clause and are recorded as later events with before and after text: EO 9323 (March 31, 1943) restated the paragraph; EO 10444 (April 10, 1953) restated it again; and EO 14085, section 2 (October 3, 2022) struck and inserted words. The OFR catalog record for EO 8809 reads 'Amended by: EO 9323, March 31, 1943; EO 10444, April 10, 1953 | See: Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163)'. Both Amended by notes are addressed as later events. The See note is a cross reference to a Secretary of Defense transfer order whose text is not held; it is not a revocation note, it predates EO 10444 (which already names the Secretary of the Air Force), and I do not treat it as ending or changing the order. EO 14085, which the catalog does not list, is found in held texts and in the U.S. Code note. Search of held texts for the number EO 8809 finds the order, EO 9323, EO 10444 (and the duplicate page text under EO 10445 and EO 9324), EO 14085 and the 1989 codification; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog report machine hits (the OFR catalog amendment notes for EO 9323 and EO 10444, the text of EO 14085, and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note prints the order as amended by EO 9323, EO 10444 and EO 14085 section 2, as current text; the printed current text matches the text as restated by EO 10444 and amended by EO 14085. The order's own text states no end date or condition. Substance changed across the restatements; a reviewer should read the before and after wording in the later events. The clause is operative as of 2026-10-14.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
-Executive Order 11298
PRESCRIBING THE INTEREST RATE FOR DEPOSIT OF SAVINGS OF  
MEMBERS OF THE UNIFORMED SERVICES
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 1035 of Title 10 of  
the United States Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966,1  
hereby prescribe that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed  
services under that Section shall accrue interest at the rate of ten  
percent per annum, compounded quarterly.
This order shall be effective September 1,1966.
